labels.label: theo:universality_tori
labels.notes: Unmarked, status partial: correct. Corrected forms unchanged and faithful (Lean >= corrected paper, every added hypothesis named): universality_tori_of_ergodic, universality_tori, universality_tori_iff (now for the family of l2ToroidalModel, an AffineToroidalModel; rich by isRichToroidalModel_l2ToroidalModel), isKernelErgodic_torusUniformKernel_iff. Printed form: UniversalityToriPrinted d (l.1141) = for every p, linear parts A with det = +-1 and every AffineToroidalModel M whose moves meet IsPrintedToriCondition at every parameter, affineToroidalFamily A M = range (M.flow A) is eps-universal. AffineToroidalModel (l.863) is l.288's object: a non-empty parameter type, translations b theta, a softmax head (measurable, > 0, summing to 1, which is what a softmax outputs), a scalar head f theta read as the outflow density clipped at 0 with finite mass (what GenerativeFlow needs); flow theta is eq. (forward_policy) with these moves and outflow f theta lambda. Nothing in the structure is stronger than the paper's 'model having a softmax head and a scalar head' (restrictions only shrink the class, which weakens the Prop and so strengthens its refutation); the empty family is excluded (affineToroidalFamily_nonempty). IsPrintedToriCondition (l.1131) is l.820 verbatim: forall i exists j with Phi_j = Phi_i^-1, and not BGConditionII of the linear parts of the generated group. The conclusion is the eps-form, weaker than Definition 3.2, and omits 'EGF' (topological ergodicity), also weaker: both strengthen the refutation. 'At every parameter' is the weakest hypothesis reading and is disclosed (REPORT question 1, SCOPE l.73-74); since Theta is non-empty, the 'at some parameter' Prop implies the 'every parameter' one, so not_universalityToriPrinted refutes it as well, as the closer says. Degenerate models: yes, a one-point model (Theta = Unit, alpha = 1/p, f = 0) refutes UniversalityToriPrinted under the same hypothesis (auditor's probe, through not_isUniversalFamilyEps_of_constantHeads, deleted). That is not an encoding artefact: l.288/l.291 condition only the moves, and a one-point model is a model with a softmax head and a scalar head (trivially a continuous family). It is C-31 itself: the printed statement fails for trivial models. The informative statements are not_isUniversalFamilyEps_of_constantHeads and not_isUniversalFamilyEps_constOutflow (minor 3). Remaining gaps in the printed-form Prop are minor (findings 2-4): GL_d(Z) for SL_d(Z); l.288's 'continuous' not encoded; under translations free over all of the torus, l.820 at every parameter is never met (vacuity, undisclosed). The d = 1 results are unchanged and correct (bgConditionII_dim_one; universalityToriPrinted_one, now through M.nonempty).

answers_to_dispatch.1_printed_prop: Yes, up to minors. UniversalityToriPrinted is a faithful Prop of Theorem 3.5 as printed: the family is l.288's (the image of a model with a non-empty parameter type, translations from the parameter, a softmax head, a scalar head), 'mild technical assumptions' read as l.820's condition (IsPrintedToriCondition, verbatim), the conclusion weaker than the paper's (eps-form, no 'EGF'). Not too strong in its requirements: every field is implied by 'softmax head', 'scalar head' and 'generative flow'. Not vacuous at d >= 2 (moves meeting l.820 exist mathematically, e.g. the generators of SL_2(Z) with b = 0, not in Lean, disclosed); vacuous at d = 1, which is the C-28 (b) finding. Degenerate Theta or heads do make it false, given hex: a one-point model refutes it (auditor's probe). That is the printed statement's own defect, which conditions only the moves (C-31), not an artefact of the encoding as the empty family was, since a one-point model is a model with the two heads. So not_universalityToriPrinted certifies only that some model fails; the informative refutations are the constant-heads theorems (minor 3). The 'every parameter' reading is disclosed as a question (REPORT question 1, SCOPE). The refutation does refute 'at some parameter': with Theta non-empty, that Prop implies the 'every parameter' one. Not disclosed: under l.288 read strictly (translations free over all of (T^d)^p), l.820 at every parameter is never met for d >= 1, so the printed theorem in that combination is vacuous rather than false (minor 3). Also not disclosed: GL_d(Z) in the Prop (minor 2) and 'continuous family' not encoded (minor 3).

findings.where: REPORT.json labels[0] (theo:universality_tori) findings[2] ('a spectral radius < 1, which summable L2-mixing needs, requires aperiodicity, which the minimal four moves lack (C-28 (a), C-30)') and corrections[0] (C-28) notes ('aperiodicity being needed only for a spectral radius < 1, i.e. for summable mixing'); not in the Lean
findings.what: A false mathematical claim in a finding about the paper, written to be carried into C-28 (AUDIT-1 suggested both this sentence and aligning C-28 (a) with it; the error is the round-1 auditor's, adopted verbatim). Aperiodicity is Bekka-Guivarc'h's sufficient condition for 'gap iff r(U0(mu)) < 1' (bg.txt l.57-60), not a necessary one, and the minimal four moves have spectral radius < 1 although they are periodic. (a) With b = 0: L2_0(T^2) is the permutation representation of SL_2(Z) on Z^2 minus 0, whose stabilizers (conjugates of the unipotent group, isomorphic to Z) are amenable. So it is weakly contained in the regular representation, and the norm of the uniform operator on S^{+-1}, T^{+-1} is at most Kesten's rho < 1 (SL_2(Z) is not amenable): spectrum in [-rho, rho]. (b) In general under l.820, given Theorem 5: if z with |z| = 1 lay in the spectrum, it would be approximate point spectrum, and by uniform convexity U(Phi_i) xi_n - z xi_n -> 0 for each move. Then h -> c_h with U(h) xi_n ~ c_h xi_n is a character of H, and K = ker c (normal, abelian quotient) has almost invariant vectors in L2_0, so it satisfies (ii) by Theorem 5. Then H satisfies (ii): with W' the intersection of the finitely many distinct p_a(h)W, the K-projection on Q^d/W' is a quotient of a subgroup of a finite product of conjugates of an amenable group, and the H-projection extends it by an abelian group. That contradicts l.820. So for affine torus actions violating (ii), l.818's gap holds in C-30's two-sided sense, with no aperiodicity, and the step C-28 (a) flags has a short fill. Told to the author as written, the sentence says the paper's l.818 -> l.273 -> Theorem 3.4 route fails at the minimal four moves, which is false.
findings.fix: In finding 3 replace the clause after the semicolon with: 'Bekka-Guivarc'h's criterion for a spectral radius < 1 (which summable L2-mixing needs) assumes the generating measure aperiodic, which the minimal four moves are not (C-28 (a)). The two-sided gap nevertheless holds there, and for every group of affine maps violating (ii): an eigenvalue of modulus 1 would give a character whose kernel has almost invariant vectors, hence satisfies (ii), hence so does the group. Not formalized and not used.' Make the same change in the C-28 note. For the master, outside this closer's paths: C-30's registered sentence 'needs the generating measure aperiodic before l.273 applies' and C-28 (a) carry a milder form of the same over-statement.

findings.where: scaffold/EGFScaffold/TorusFamilies.lean:859-876 (AffineToroidalModel docstring), :63-80 (SCOPE); REPORT labels[0] questions[1] ('translations (free parameters)') and the C-31 note ('the empty family is no longer available')
findings.what: Three facts about the reading of l.288 are not disclosed. (a) AffineToroidalModel lets the translations be any function of theta, constants included, and the Prop's refutation uses constant translations (constToroidalModelAt). Under l.288 read strictly (all translation parts free, as in constToroidalModel), l.820 cannot hold at every parameter for d >= 1. For each i the set of translations where some Phi_j is Phi_i^-1 is a finite union of proper closed subgroups unless A_i = -I, so inverse-stability fails somewhere. If every A_i = -I, the linear parts {+-I} satisfy (ii). So in that combination the printed theorem is vacuous, not refuted, and the 'every parameter' reading needs models that tie the translations (fixed, l.697; in inverse pairs, l.293), which the structure allows. The REPORT's 'translations (free parameters)' says the opposite of what the refutation uses. (b) l.288's 'continuous family' is not encoded (no topology on Theta, no measurability of f), so the Lean class is larger. The witnesses are continuous, so the refutation is unaffected. (c) A one-point model refutes UniversalityToriPrinted under the same hypothesis (auditor's probe, deleted: Theta = Unit, alpha = 1/p, f = 0, through not_isUniversalFamilyEps_of_constantHeads). So not UniversalityToriPrinted certifies only 'some model fails', the printed statement's own triviality (C-31). The C-31 note's 'the empty family is no longer available' reads as if the refutation were now informative about models.
findings.fix: In REPORT question 2 and SCOPE: 'translations are a function of the parameter (free, tied in inverse pairs, or fixed); with all translations free, l.820 cannot hold at every parameter, so the every-parameter reading is refuted through models that tie them'; 'continuity (l.288) is not encoded; the refuting models are continuous'; and in the C-31 note: 'a one-point model refutes it as well; the informative statements are not_isUniversalFamilyEps_of_constantHeads and not_isUniversalFamilyEps_constOutflow'.
